study type: Cross-sectional study (secondary analysis of survey data)
exposure: Type of institution (private vs. public hospitals)
cohort: A nationally representative sample of 7760 births in India from the National Family Health Survey (2019-21), including 5965 repeated C-sections.
finding: Maternal age over 35 years, a higher wealth index, and undergoing ultrasonography were significantly associated with increased odds of repeated C-section deliveries in India, with private facilities showing a higher prevalence than public facilities.
mod_finding: Repeated C-section deliveries occurred in 78% of births in the study cohort, with private hospitals accounting for 79% and public healthcare facilities 76% of these deliveries.
